rows.statement: Adults should sleep 7 or more hours per night on a regular basis (lower bound of the recommended nightly sleep for adults 18 to 60).
rows.validFor: adults aged 18 to 60, guidance current at 2026-11-26

sources.citation: Watson NF et al., 'Recommended Amount of Sleep for a Healthy Adult: A Joint Consensus Statement of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine and Sleep Research Society', Sleep 2015;38(6):843-844, doi 10.5665/sleep.4716
sources.quote: Adults should sleep 7 or more hours per night on a regular basis to promote optimal health.

sources.citation: American Academy of Sleep Medicine, 'Adult Sleep Duration Health Advisory' (adopted 2014-02-17, updated 2015-08-14)
sources.quote: recommends that adults should sleep 7 or more hours per night on a regular basis to promote optimal health

sources.citation: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, 'About Sleep' (2024-05-15), recommended sleep table

rows.notes: Backs the floor of career.life.sleepNeedHours (E7.4.1). The bible's 7.5 h need is a design value inside the recommended range; the test checks it never drops below this row.

statusHistory.reason: G-53: three read sources in three independence groups, one primary

rows.statement: Working 55 or more hours a week is associated with an estimated 35% higher risk of stroke and 17% higher risk of dying from ischemic heart disease, compared with 35 to 40 hours a week (WHO and ILO joint estimate). Value is the weekly-hours threshold.
rows.validFor: WHO/ILO global estimate published 2021-05-17 (Environment International study)

sources.citation: World Health Organization and International Labour Organization, 'Long working hours increasing deaths from heart disease and stroke: WHO, ILO', news release 2021-05-17
sources.quote: is associated with an estimated 35% higher risk of a stroke and a 17% higher risk of dying from ischemic heart disease

sources.citation: NPR, 'Overwork Killed More Than 745,000 People In A Year, WHO Study Finds', 2021-05-17
sources.quote: face an estimated 35% higher risk of a stroke and a 17% higher risk of dying from heart disease

sources.citation: American Industrial Hygiene Association, 'ILO and WHO: Long Working Hours Can Increase Deaths from Heart Disease, Stroke', 2021-05-20
sources.quote: Working 55 or more hours per week is associated with an estimated 35 percent higher risk of stroke

rows.notes: Backs the light/normal cut of the E8.1.1 load bands (the bible's starting cut point is the same 55 h). It is evidence that long hours carry health risk; it does not set the yearly health-step chances, which stay design values. NPR and AIHA report the WHO release; they say 'heart disease' where WHO says 'ischemic heart disease'.

statusHistory.reason: G-53: primary release plus two independent reports
